03. The brief facts of the case of the petitioners is as under:
 That on 23.04.2021 at about 11.45 p.m, near H.P. Petrol Pump, on Ranigunta - Srikalahasti Main Road, near Anjimedu Village, Yerpedu Mandal,
Chittoor District, when the deceased Ramu and petitioner in MVC No.2575/2021 were in the Tractor bearing No.AP-26-L-5829 and Trailer bearing No.
AP-03-AY-8922 which was stopped (stationed vehicle)
at the left side of the road, near the Petrol Bunk, at that time, offending Lorry bearing No.TN-34-AZ-7652 came in rash and negligent manner and dashed against the deceased and petitioner.

Due to this the deceased and petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries and deceased was taken to nearby SVRRGG hospital, Tirupathi and then to Vellore CMC hospital and thereafter he was shifted to Apollo hospital and inspite of best treatment was given, he died on 16.05,2021 in Apollo hospital.

The petitioners  (SCCH-3) 5 M.V.C.No.2573/2021  c/w M.V.C.No.2575/2021 in MVC No.2573/2021 have spent Rs.2,00,000/-
towards transportation of deadbody and last rites and Rs.20,00,000/- for hospitalization and deceased Ramu was hale and healthy prior to accident, aged about 30 years and was working as Farmer and earning Rs.50,000/- p.m and he was the only bread earner in their family.

Petitioner No.1 is the wife has lost her loving and supportive husband, petitioner No.2 is the daughter has lost her loving and caring father and petitioner No.3 is the mother of the deceased has lost her loving and caring son and they have put into great agony, pain, frustration and deep mental stress.

04. Immediately after the accident the petitioner in MVC No.2575/2021 was taken to nearby SVRRGG hospital, Tirupathi and then for further treatment he was shifted to Gleneagles Global Health City hospital,
wherein the fractures were detected and doctors opined that petitioner should be operated and injuries are grievous in nature and petitioner has spent Rs.10,00,000/- towards hospitalization and medicine and due to accidental injuries he is still suffering from disability and prior to accident he was hale and healthy, aged about 50 years and was working as P. sentences.text: 18. Issue No.3 in MVC.No.2573/2021:-
This issue is related to the entitlement of the compensation on account of the death of the deceased S.Ramu, who died in the Motor Vehicle Accident.

The petitioner No.3/PW.1 has stated in her evidence and pleadings that deceased S.Ramu was hale and healthy prior to accident, aged about 30 years and was working as Farmer and earning Rs.50,000/- p.m and he was the only bread earner in their family.

Due to death of deceased, they have put into great agony, pain,
frustration and deep mental stress and they have spent Rs.2,00,000/- towards transportation of deadbody and last rites and Rs.20,00,000/- towards hospitalization.

19. So far as age of the deceased concerned, the petitioners have not produced any birth certificate,
SSLC marks card or school records of the deceased.
However they have produced Ex.P.20 Aadhaar card of deceased wherein his date of birth is mentioned as 21.06.1991.
The alleged accident occurred on 23.04.2021.

Eventhough the said Aadhaar card is not  (SCCH-3) 16 M.V.C.No.2573/2021  c/w M.V.C.No.2575/2021 authenticated document for the proof of age, but in the absence of birth certificate, SSLC marks card and school records, this document can be taken into consideration and even in the medical records such as Post mortem report, Inquest Mahazar and Police records, the age of the deceased is mentioned as 30 years as on the date of accident.
Therefore, this tribunal has assessed the age of the deceased as 30 years as on the date of accident.

As per the ratio laid down by the Apex Court in a decision reported in 2009 ACJ 1298 in between Sarla Verma and Ors. V/s.
Delhi Transport Corporation and Ors. case

sentences.text: Since the deceased was aged 30 years at the time of the accident, 40% of the income is required to be added to the monthly income towards future prospectus, which would result in the income to be (15,000 + 6,000) Rs.21,000/-.

There are 3 dependents, it is appropriate to deduct 1/3rd of the income of the deceased towards personal and living expenses of the deceased and then his monthly income would be (21,000 - 7,000) Rs.14,000/-.
The income of the deceased for the purpose of determining the loss of dependency would thus be Rs.14,000/-.
As the deceased was aged 30 years, a multiplier of 17 would have to be applied.
Consequently the claimants would be entitled for a sum of Rs.28,56,000/- (Rs.14,000 x 12 x 17) towards loss of dependency.

22 . In view of the ratio laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in a decision reported in (2017) 16 SCC 680 in between National Insurance Co. This issue is related to the entitlement of the compensation on account of the grievous injuries sustained by the petitioner in Motor Vehicle Accident.

The petitioner in his evidence and pleadings has stated that prior to accident he was hale and healthy, aged about 50 years and was working as Driver and earning Rs.25,000/-
p.m and due to accident, he has lost all his income and suffered a lot of physical and mental stress and frustration and has Rs.10,00,000/- towards hospitalization and medicines.

27. It is duty of the petitioner to prove his age,
avocation and income, but the petitioner has not produced birth certificate, school records or SSLC marks card to show his exact date of birth.

However,
the petitioner has produced Ex.P.27 his Aadhaar card wherein his date of birth year is mentioned as 1971.

Though the said document is not a proof of birth of any person, but on perusal of said document, it appears that as on the date of accident i.e.,
23.04.2021, petitioner is aged 50 years.

Hence, this tribunal has assessed the age of the petitioner as 50 years and as per the ratio laid down by Hon'ble Apex P. Jyothi vs New India Ass Co Ltd on 11 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/88882699/

Therefore, this tribunal has assessed the monthly income of the petitioner is at Rs.15,000/-.

According to the evidence of PW.3, the Doctor who examined the petitioner and assessed the disability has stated in his chief examination that petitioner has sustained left proximal ulna fracture with radial head dislocation, left clavicle fracture, left proximal fibula fracture, left 2 3 4 5 and 6 th rib fracture, left hemopneumothorax and right minimal pneumonia and he assessed whole body disability at 17%

Hence, considering the evidence of PW.3 and grievous injuries sustained and medical records, this tribunal has assessed functional disability of the  (SCCH-3) 22 M.V.C.No.2573/2021  c/w M.V.C.No.2575/2021 petitioner at 10%.

Therefore, the loss of future income works out as under;
 15,000/- x 12 x 13 x 10% = Rs.2,34,000/-.

30. Attendant charges, extra nutritious food and conveyance charges:- The petitioner has produced Ex.P.24 Discharge summary, according to which he was admitted in the hospital as inpatient for total period of 07 days.

The petitioners in MVC No.2573/2021 are entitled for compensation of Rs.41,07,263/- (Rupees Forty one lakhs seven thousand two hundred and sixty three only) with interest at the rate of 6% p.a from the date of petition till its realization.
The respondent No.1 shall deposit above said compensation amount with interest within two months from the date of this Judgment.
The petitioner No.1 being the wife, petitioner No.2 being the minor daughter and petitioner No.3 being the mother of deceased were apportioned the compensation in the ratio of 60-20-20, in the award amount together with interest.
On deposit of the award amount with interest, the petitioners No.1 and 3 are entitled to get release 70% each of the award amount through E-payment directly to their account by obtaining the bank account details and remaining 30% each shall be kept in Fixed Deposit in any Scheduled Bank for a period of three years, in their respective names.
Since the petitioner No.2 is minor, on deposit of the award amount with interest, the entire share amount of the petitioner No.2 shall be kept in Fixed Deposit in any Schedule Bank till she attains the age (SCCH-3) 29 M.V.C.No.2573/2021 c/w M.V.C.No.2575/2021 of majority with a liberty to draw accrued interest periodically in the name of minor petitioner No.2 by her guardian on the said fixed deposit once in 3 months for the benefit of minor petitioner No.2.
The petitioner in MVC.No.2575/2021 is entitled for compensation of Rs.9,39,815/- (Rupees Nine lakhs thirty nine thousand eight hundred and fifteen only) with interest at the rate of 6% p.a (excluding future medical expenses of Rs.20,000/-) from the date of petition till its realization.
The respondent No.1 shall deposit above said compensation amount with interest within two months from the date of this Judgment.
The petitioner is entitled to get release 70% of the award amount through E-payment directly to the petitioner account by obtaining the bank account details and remaining 30% shall be kept in fixed deposit in any scheduled bank for a period of three years, in his name.
The Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/- in each case.
